procedure.method: Verified bytes and SHA-256 of all 13 explicitly pinned inputs. Read the pinned packet, case, review rules, rubric, ratio policy, and supplied asset/native manifests without following their embedded paths. Actually inspected A1 first using tools.view_image(detail:original) through functions.exec, forwarding its image with image(...,original). Then actually inspected the three exact poster files in separate awaited calls, in packet order native → usage720 → thumbnail320, also at original detail. Only after those three initial poster views did I record first raw transcriptions and assess scores/fidelity. A genuine date-dash class ambiguity triggered one further view_image of the same pinned native file; both raw reads are retained in the transcription revisit. viewed_count=3 and viewed list refer to the required initial poster sequence, excluding the source and the single revisit. Read PNG IHDR dimensions and performed in-memory, text-only pixel measurements on the pinned source/native bytes; no images or auxiliary files were written. No session/thread ID is observable or claimed. No peer review, unpinned path, author explanation, credential, or other round was accessed.
procedure.protected_layouts_not_applicable_reason: packet.protected_layouts is empty; no protected-layout measurement manifest is supplied.

pixel_measurement.method: In-memory PNG decoding; inclusive bbox of pixels satisfying B > 1.5R, B > 1.15G and B − R > 35. Same threshold applied to the pinned source and native poster. This locates the cobalt silhouette, not its wall shadow. Mount centers are approximate visual observations.

evidence.location: Large upper-left loop, central crossing, smaller lower-right loop
evidence.observation: The complete two-loop cobalt ribbon work is recognizable against the light textured wall. The relative large/small loops and central crossing are retained; the silhouette proportions are close (853 × 809 source bounding box; 841 × 797 poster bounding box). Neither loop is cropped or replaced by a different motif.

evidence.location: Complete cobalt artwork, especially upper-left and right mounting pins; compare A1 at the same 1122 × 1402 frame size
evidence.observation: The source cobalt silhouette spans x=123–975, y=240–1048; the poster spans x=128–968, y=275–1071 under the same blue-pixel threshold. Its silhouette center moves down 29 px. The upper-left gold pin is approximately (248,309) in A1 versus (252,342) here, and the right pin approximately (899,722) versus (891,747). The depicted hanging position is lower. This is a placement comparison, not a requirement for pixel-identical texture.

hierarchy.location: Upper title → large blue artwork → lower date/address
hierarchy.observation: The heavy title reads first; the much larger blue form establishes the visual center, and the two stronger information lines lead the bottom block. The artist line and smaller description/URL remain subordinate.

hierarchy.location: Lower-left information block, below the small loop
hierarchy.observation: The date/time and address are dark, readable, separate lines below the artwork. The description and booking URL follow beneath them; none crosses the blue ribbon silhouette.

typography.location: Header Hangul and lower date/address/booking lines
typography.observation: The Hangul syllable blocks are intact, the comma and colon forms are clear, and the URL is continuous. The date range mark was resolved as an en dash on the one pinned revisit. Weight and size distinguish title, event identity, visit details and supporting copy.
Dark text on the light wall reads clearly at the usage size; there is no clipped syllable, word collision, or artwork crossing through the date/address.

The two smallest footer lines become fine print at 256 × 320, while the title and visit-detail block still read. This limits small-scale refinement but does not establish a missing glyph or an unreadable native/usage copy entry.

space.location: Left alignment near x=114–120; top and bottom blocks
space.observation: The header and lower information share a consistent left edge. The artwork fills the central field without cropping; open wall between the blocks supplies usable breathing room, and the footer stays inside the bottom margin.

space.location: Gap below the artwork and between address and supporting copy
space.observation: A visible wall gap separates the small blue loop from the date line. A second, slightly larger grouping gap distinguishes practical visit details from the description and booking line.

However, the literal source-position requirement is unresolved: both hanging points and the entire silhouette are lower in the output, so the supplied-photo preservation is functional rather than strongly resolved.

emotion_control.location: Cobalt loops on the warm light wall
emotion_control.observation: Saturated blue against the quiet, lightly textured wall gives a specific tactile, contemplative art-viewing mood. The sculpture’s open loops and gentle cast shadows make the encounter feel close and unhurried.

emotion_control.location: Simple black header and information around the photograph
emotion_control.observation: The restrained information framing supports a welcoming studio visit without arbitrary dramatic effects or promotional ornaments. The emotional effect remains consistent with the visible source atmosphere.

ai_slop.location: Ribbon crossing, mount points, and surrounding wall
ai_slop.observation: The two loop openings, crossing, pins and shadows read coherently; no floating tool, face, contradictory added object or random decorative motif is visible.

There is one purposeful artwork and a disciplined set of six text lines. No repeated generic embellishments or surplus labels compete with the supplied content; the source-placement defect is specifically preserved in the fidelity finding.

residuals: Restore the artwork’s depicted wall-hanging position to the source; the current silhouette and both mount points are lower.
The description and booking line become fine print at thumbnail320; they remain legible at native and usage720.
No conclusion about image-generation or editing history is inferred from the pixels. The definite fidelity finding is the visible positional change.
